catalog_quote: The phonological foot in Kubokota consists of two syllables. Words are parsed from left to right; any syllables at the right edge of the word that cannot be assigned to feet are extrametrical. Primary stress falls on the rightmost foot. Thus in two- and three-syllable words, stress falls on the first syllable. Two-syllable words constitute a single foot; three-syllable words a foot plus an extrametrical final syllable. (10) /ˈmane/ 'basket' /ˈsi.e/ 'dog' /ˈnunu/ 'earthquake' /ˈβa.e/ 'flood'; /ˈlikoto/ 'bushknife' /ˈkoburu/ > [ˈkomburu] 'child' /ˈboɣuzu/ 'big.wave' /ˈmatoβa/ 'landslide' ... In words consisting of four or more syllables, secondary stress falls on the first syllable with stress on every alternate syllable to the right, and primary stress on the rightmost foot. new_statements.rule_in_words: Quantity-insensitive trochaic feet built left to right; a leftover final syllable is extrametrical; primary stress on the head of the rightmost foot. Result: initial stress in 2- and 3-syllable words (the bulk of the lexicon), penultimate in 4-syllable words, antepenultimate (third syllable) in 5-syllable words; position depends on syllable-count parity rather than a fixed edge.
new_statements.secondary_stress: In words of four or more syllables, secondary stress on the first syllable and every alternate syllable to the right (heads of non-final feet); disyllabic prefix /vari-/ RECIP forms its own foot with secondary stress; with polysyllabic enclitics on roots longer than two syllables, a secondary foot is aligned to the left edge of the root.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllabic prefixes /ta-/ PASS and /pa-/ CAUS are unstressed unless two or more prefixes can form a foot; after /vari-/ the causative /pa-/ is extrametrical and stress falls on the first root syllable even if the root is monosyllabic; monosyllabic subject markers unstressed, polysyllabic ones (or those hosting =ke NEG) form a phonological word and are stressed normally; monosyllabic enclitics/suffixes (-i TR, applicatives, some object/possessor enclitics) count as part of the phonological word; polysyllabic enclitics form a foot and take primary stress. Vowel sequences are separate syllables with stress on the first vowel.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (root plus monosyllabic suffixes/enclitics; polysyllabic subject markers and enclitics form their own feet); citation forms with primary and secondary stress marks given.
new_statements.identity_note: Chambers describes Kubokota, the variety of the east coast / northern half of Ranongga Island. She states (p. 21) that Kubokota and Ganoqa (= Ghanongga, the Glottolog/ISO name, ghan1242 / ghn) were dialect areas of one language, Ganoqa on the west coast, and that the Ganoqa variety is probably no longer spoken, its former speakers having shifted to Kubokota. Glottolog ghan1242 has no separate dialect code for Kubokota; the statement applies to ghan1242 as the Kubokota dialect.
